# Metric library

Define each number goals are measured by once (its meaning and calculation, unit, direction, source and owner), and say which metric measures a goal, for a team or the whole company.

Module id `metrics`, in [src/modules/metrics/](../../../src/modules/metrics/module.json).

## What it adds to the core

| Extension point | What |
|---|---|
| Needs | none |
| Routes | `/metrics`, `/metrics/new`, `/metrics/:metricId`, `/metrics/:metricId/edit` |
| Old addresses | `/data/metrics` → `/metrics` |
| Navigation | Metrics |
| Places on core screens | `goal.facts`, `goal.measure`, `goal.sections`, `people.person`, `people.team` |
| Workspace sections | none |
| Database tables | `okr_metrics` (0033_metric_library.sql): The metric library: one row per metric, never deleted (removed_at when removed).; `okr_goal_metrics` (0033_metric_library.sql): Which metric measures a goal, and for which slice (a team, or the whole company when team_id is null): one row per goal, removed_at when unlinked. |
| Its own records | metric (`okr_metrics`, filed under `modules.metrics.metrics`; removable and restorable); metric link (`okr_goal_metrics`, filed under `modules.metrics.metricLinks`) |

## Requirements

- `METRICS-LIBRARY`: Anyone can find a metric, read what it means, and see every goal measured by it side by side (ML1). Metrics (/metrics, in the menu after People; on a phone under More) lists every metric in use A to Z ignoring case and accents, 50 a page; a search matches the name, unit, "lower is better" or "higher is better", the owner and the meaning; filters for the unit, the team or the whole company a goal measures it for, the owner, which way is better, no goals, and something to sort out; sorts A to Z, most goals first and changed lately; everything in the address. A row links to the metric, says its unit, direction and owner, and its goals by status as shape and word, worst first. A metric's page says what it means and how it's calculated, then its goals as a table (status, goal, for, now, target with its week, against plan, owner), worst first, with the lowest and highest now when two or more have a number, then its source, the source's owner, refresh, caveats and who added and last changed it. Its owner and admins see what it still needs and can change or remove it; everyone else sees who can. A goal's summary says what measures it; a person's page lists the metrics they own and a team's the metrics its goals use. Old addresses under /data/metrics lead to the library, a metric or the form. (Copy.)
- `METRICS-MEASURED-BY`: A goal's metric is chosen by typing to find it where the goal is made or changed, or added there, and fills in what the metric already says (ML2). In New goal, "Measured by" is the first field on the measure step (under the name when changing a goal), never for a goal with dated stages or for someone who may not link the goal: find-and-pick with "No metric" first, metrics in the goal's unit offered first, and "Add “…” as a new metric" last. Choosing one shows its meaning, the goal's team or the whole company under "For", and, on a new goal whose unit and decimals nobody typed, sets them from the metric and says so in one line with "Use different ones". A unit that differs stops the save with the reason. Added in place, a metric needs a name, a unit and which way is better, is owned by whoever adds it, and is chosen. Check says "Measured by {metric}, for {team}". Goals filters by the metric (?metric=, "Measured by" in the filter line), and a metric's page opens Goals filtered to it. (Copy.)
- `METRICS-CARE`: A metric's owner and admins are shown what it is missing; removing or changing one says what happens to its goals (ML3). A metric's page lists, for its owner and admins only, what it still needs in order (no owner, no meaning, no source, no goal after 14 days), each with a button that opens the form at that field. Adding a metric whose name is close to one in use (one name's words contain the other's, or they share two words and differ by one, leaving out filler words and brackets) asks "This looks like …" as a Check (METRIC-DEFINED), with Use that one or Mine is different: keep it. The form keeps a draft through Close, Back and a reload; each error shows under its field once the field is left or on the first try to save, and the first field in error takes the focus. Changing the unit or direction of a metric goals use asks first, saying how many goals and how many will show a warning. Remove says which goals stop being measured (a stopped goal's too); Undo puts the metric and its links back, and Put it back later restores the links it had to goals still there. Workspace → About tells admins how many metrics have no owner, with See them. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-DEFINED`: A metric can be used with a name, a unit and a direction; what it still lacks is said in words, never scored; and a likely mistake in its name, unit or meaning is questioned before it is saved (MT1). Add a metric asks for Name, Unit (with Decimal places, optional, 0 if left) and Which way is better, then what it means, then, under "Where the number comes from · can be said later", its source, who owns that source and how often it refreshes, then its owner and caveats. A Must fix shows under its field outlined and washed with the warning mark and "Must fix"; a Check under its field with the warning mark, "Check" and its answers as plain buttons; neither uses a status shape. The foot says "{a} to fix, {b} to check." and the completeness line. The Checks: a name one letter (two for names over 12 characters; never for 4 or fewer) or a word from another metric's, or one a metric used to have; a unit spelt differently from one in use; a percentage or rate whose meaning doesn't say out of what. Saving is refused while a Must fix stands, and with a Check unanswered it scrolls to it and says "Answer the question above first."; an answered Check closes to one line with Change. A metric's page says "Fully defined" or "Still to say: …" (and "Its owner has left.") under its title, for everyone, with each item a link to the form's field for its owner and admins. get_metric returns the line; save_metric returns unanswered checks without saving and takes answers. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-PARTS`: A goal is measured by a metric for a team or the whole company and optionally one part of that number, takes the metric's unit and direction, and says why when what measures it changes after check-ins (MT2). "Measured by" shows "From the metric" ({unit}, {decimals in words}, {direction}, and where the number comes from) and, under For, "Which part" (optional, at most 60 characters), with the parts other goals on the metric use offered under it. A part spelt like one in use (the same once case, accents, punctuation and a trailing s are set aside, or one edit away; never for two characters) is a Check (Use it / Keep yours); another live goal on the same metric, team and part is a Check (Carry on). On a goal with check-ins, changing its metric, For or part needs Why, which its History entry gives. A goal's About lists Measured by: For, What it means, From the metric, Where the number comes from, Caveats, This goal's own and, when it differs from the metric's meaning, For this goal. A metric's page shows each goal's For with its part. link_goal_metric takes part and reason, returns checks and saves nothing until it gets answers. (Copy.)
- `METRIC-CHANGE`: A metric that changes tells its goals (MT3). Changing a metric goals use reads back what it does to them first: a new meaning or source asks "Is it still the same number?"; "The number itself changes" and a new direction each need a reason, and leave a mark on every goal's chart ("Definition changed, week {w}", a dashed hairline labelled beside it) and History; a new unit is a new label (every goal's unit changes too) or a different scale, refused. A metric that has measured a goal is retired, not deleted: its goals keep their links and numbers and say "Measured by {metric}, retired {date}", it leaves the pickers, and Bring it back undoes it. Admins merge a metric into another in the same unit, moving its goals and retiring it pointing there. Every one of these saves with one Undo, and retire_metric, merge_metrics and save_metric's comparable, reason and relabel do the same through MCP. (Copy.)

## Help

- **Metrics: what each number means** (`metrics`): The metric library: each number goals are measured by, defined once, with its page saying what it means and every goal measured by it, side by side.
- **Defining a metric well** (`metric-define`): A metric needs three things to be used: a name, a unit and which way is better. The rest can be said later, and its page says what is still to say, in words, never as a score.
- **Measured by: choosing a goal’s metric** (`metric-measured-by`): In New goal and when changing a goal, say which metric measures it by typing to find one, or add one there.
- **Measured by: for whom, and which part** (`metric-slices`): What a goal takes from its metric and what stays its own, whose number it is, and one part of that number.
- **Changing, retiring and merging a metric** (`metric-change`): Which changes save at once, the ones that tell a metric’s goals first, and retiring, bringing back and merging.
